situation:
You are a warehouse worker in your early twenties supporting a younger sibling on a single income. Two employers have offered you a job, and you have to answer both this week. The financial coach (judge) at BRIARWOOD FAMILY FINANCIAL CENTER has agreed to help you compare them.

Last month a phishing text reached your bank account, and you put the replacement costs on a credit card while the bank investigated. The card issuer charges interest every month the balance sits there. Social Security comes out of every paycheck, along with the taxes that pay for your sibling's school, and beyond that you have nothing set aside for retirement.

One offer pays a higher hourly wage with no retirement match and no paid sick days. Taking it would clear the credit card balance faster, but nothing would be set aside for retirement and a sick day would cost you a full day's pay. The other offer pays a lower wage with a retirement match and paid sick days, though the smaller paycheck means carrying the card balance for months and paying far more in interest.

Your sibling depends on this single income for school costs and food, and a week of unpaid illness would fall on them too. The financial coach (judge) wants your recommendation on which offer to accept and how you will handle the card balance. The financial coach (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the financial coach (judge) at BRIARWOOD FAMILY FINANCIAL CENTER. The background is the same as the situation above.

You have agreed to help a young worker decide between the offer with the higher hourly wage and no paid sick days and the offer with the lower wage, the retirement match and paid sick days, and to hear how the credit card balance will be handled either way.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and after the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what will this choice have changed about your savings?
If you stay with this employer for ten years, what will you have for retirement?
